page: Vultr voc-s-2c-16gb-320s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under a shared CPU allocation model. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the processor is equipped with 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, and includes 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU resources are present.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the top 10%, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression results. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the average tier, and overall PassMark CPU metrics, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests, rank in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed; while large-block read and write bandwidths are average, small-block cached read bandwidth is weak. Database and transactional workloads show limitations, with PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations both placing in the bottom 25%, and static web serving throughput registering in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1 and substantial local NVMe SSD storage relative to its compute footprint. This makes it a resource-dense option for workloads that require moderate memory capacity and fast local storage without demanding sustained, dedicated multi-core CPU performance. Due to the shared CPU allocation and weaker multi-threaded and database benchmark results, it is less suited for high-throughput database hosting or intensive web serving. Instead, the instance is appropriate for memory-intensive background tasks, single-threaded processing pipelines, lightweight caching layers, and development environments requiring fast local disk access.

Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor operates at 2.0 GHz and supports AVX-512 and AES instruction sets. Benchmark data reveals top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng and strong single-threaded compression speeds, though multi-core CPU metrics, database operations, and static web serving throughput fall into lower percentiles.
